without_examples.reasoning: The intent clearly specifies a latency sweep (20, 80, 150 ms) over a fixed 25 Mbps link for two applications: YouTube and Zoom. This maps to an application comparison crossed with a latency sweep. Per system prompt rules, since two distinct applications are mentioned, the design MUST include at least one concurrent experiment where both run simultaneously. I therefore include: (1) isolated experiments for each application at each latency point (a 2-app × 3-latency = 6-experiment grid), and (2) concurrent experiments where YouTube and Zoom share the 25 Mbps link at each latency (3 more experiments), for 9 total. No CC algorithm was specified, so cubic (default) will be used. No AQM was specified, so fq_codel (default) will be used. No cross-traffic was specified, so ctp_cluster is null (clean baseline). Duration will use per-application defaults: 60s for YouTube and 120s for Zoom; concurrent runs will use the longer of the two (120s). The latency sweep will stress-test Zoom especially at 150 ms (approaching the 300 ms warning threshold for real-time apps) and YouTube at 150 ms (well within comfortable range). The design_type list reflects: isolated (YouTube+Zoom separate sweeps) and concurrent (both together), summarized here as the three design intents present in the full experiment set.
